reviewers.required_before: phase b enrols any real account
phase c retires the server-held keys
phase a changes any user-facing promise (with B01 and B11)
phase d moves any feature into the vault

rejected.reason: The operator reads every journal entry; contradicts the owner's premise.
Truthful but operator-readable; the owner rejected the dossier's 'A for beta' recommendation on 2026-10-07.
Needs vendor hardware, spend and a real attestation spike, and is not required for the stored-data guarantee; reopen trigger only.
Provider-managed custody is not operator-blind; only its vault-local inference is kept, inside BD.

phases.name: Client key generation and encrypted-sync envelope
Plaintext-needing server features move to the device or vault

open_owner_questions.question: Recovery, account reset, device pairing, revocation, double loss, death or incapacity, and malicious support requests.
Is credit-funded inference on a no-retention runtime we control, or on an ordinary-Fly vault, compatible with the premise, and how is it labelled?
Which signed or pinned web delivery mechanism, and may web accounts enrol before it ships?
Which encrypted columns are journal content (practice reflections, prompt responses, feedback, the vault credential)?
Opt-in or required enrolment, the retirement date for server-held keys, dormant accounts, and backup expiry values.
What enrolled accounts are told about server features that stop until phase d moves them.
Which reviewed primitives, envelope format and library.
Whether and when to ship native apps (store and signing accounts).
Whether web may keep a person's provider key in localStorage.
Budget per active account-month and staffing per phase.
Who the four owed reviewers are.

boundary.value: The Adepthood server process, its database and backups, Creek on ordinary Fly, and every configured model vendor all see plaintext; provider-managed custody is not operator-blind.

key_custody.value: Server env var JOURNAL_ENCRYPTION_KEYS holds every key; EncryptedString decrypts on every ORM read. No per-person key exists.

recovery.value: Operator restores from backup with the env keys; password reset restores full access.

metadata_leakage.value: Everything: content, sizes, timestamps, counts, tiers, ids, network metadata.

inference_location.value: Server-side cloud calls paid by the app's own LLM_API_KEY unless the person supplies a key; Creek reflection when a vault is bound.

supported_platforms.value: Web only ships; native is configured but unshipped.

update_trust.value: Operator-served web bundle with a report-only CSP; a modified bundle is undetectable to the person.

primary_copy_removal.value: Nothing removed: 18 EncryptedString columns across 10 tables, DERIVED_FROM_PROSE plaintext, backups, Creek copies and vendor copies all persist under operator control.

threat_actors.value: Defends a database or backup thief only while the env keys stay separate; nothing against operator, host, compelled update, subpoena or support pressure.

reopen_triggers.value: Not a selectable end state; the owner's premise rules it out.

boundary.value: Same as HEAD, with copy that says the operator can read; provider-managed custody is not operator-blind.

key_custody.value: Server-held env keys, least privilege and audit; operator trust remains.

recovery.value: Operator-assisted restore and ordinary password reset.

metadata_leakage.value: Content and all metadata are visible to the operator.

inference_location.value: Server-side, under an explicit destination policy.

supported_platforms.value: Web and any future native client equally.

update_trust.value: Not a decision input: the operator can already read stored data.

primary_copy_removal.value: None required; cleanup and honest copy only.

threat_actors.value: DB thief and backup holder only; privileged operator, host and subpoena all succeed.

reopen_triggers.value: Rejected by the owner on 2026-10-07: it contradicts the premise that the operator cannot read journal entries.

boundary.value: Stored prose is ciphertext the server cannot decrypt; the person's devices hold plaintext.

key_custody.value: Keys generated on the person's device; no operator escrow; AEAD bound to owner, object and version.

metadata_leakage.value: Sizes, timestamps, counts, object ids, tier labels and network metadata remain visible.

inference_location.value: None on the server; any AI needs a separate location (D, a vault, or BYOK).

supported_platforms.value: Native and web; web depends on trusting the served bundle.

update_trust.value: Native: store-signed builds. Web: operator-served code can exfiltrate keys unless signed or pinned delivery is built.

primary_copy_removal.value: Every server-readable copy must be re-encrypted client-side or deleted, including derived plaintext and backups.

threat_actors.value: Defeats DB thief, backup holder, host and stored-data subpoena; a malicious or compelled web update and a compromised device still succeed.

reopen_triggers.value: Selected as half of BD; reopen if a key-non-possession prototype fails.

boundary.value: Hardware-isolated runtime; the operator is excluded only if attestation and key release are proven on real hardware.

key_custody.value: User-authorized key release into a measured enclave; no operator-reusable unlock material.

metadata_leakage.value: Runtime metadata, sizes and timing remain visible to the host.

supported_platforms.value: Any client that can verify attestation.

update_trust.value: Measured image plus verifier governance; client trust problem from B persists.

primary_copy_removal.value: Same removal burden as B, plus the attestation chain.

threat_actors.value: Defeats host and operator under the hardware threat model; vendor flaws and compelled updates remain.

reopen_triggers.value: Reopen if confidential compute becomes a cheap way to give the runtime we control an operator-blind property.

boundary.value: Content never leaves the device when sync is off; with B it syncs as ciphertext.

key_custody.value: OS keystore and a local encrypted database.

metadata_leakage.value: None to the server when unsynced; B's metadata when synced.

inference_location.value: On the device, on capability-verified hardware only.

supported_platforms.value: Capable native devices; web limited by browser runtime and storage.

update_trust.value: Signed native builds; web has the same served-code problem as B.

primary_copy_removal.value: Does not by itself remove existing server copies; needs B's migration.

threat_actors.value: Defeats every remote actor for unsent content; a compromised device and a malicious update still succeed.

reopen_triggers.value: Selected as half of BD; reopen if B09 finds no supported-device configuration.

boundary.value: Per-account Fly vault and the Adepthood server both see plaintext; provider-managed custody is not operator-blind.

key_custody.value: Provider-managed keys; Fly supplies the unlock capability.

recovery.value: Provider backup and restore; no user-held guarantee.

metadata_leakage.value: Content and metadata are visible to host and operator.

update_trust.value: Not a decision input: the operator can already read stored data.

primary_copy_removal.value: Adds a copy; the Adepthood primary copy remains.

threat_actors.value: Defeats external AI vendors only; operator, host and subpoena succeed.

reopen_triggers.value: Rejected as a custody model; its vault-local inference survives inside BD for consented, non-retained processing.

boundary.value: Stored journal content and its prose derivatives are ciphertext the operator cannot decrypt. Plaintext exists on the person's devices, in a vault they choose for inference, and at a cloud vendor only under their own key, sent from the device and never relayed by our server.

key_custody.value: User-held keys generated on the person's device; no operator escrow; the server stores ciphertext and public parameters only.

metadata_leakage.value: Sizes, timestamps, counts, object ids, tier labels, credit receipts and network metadata stay visible to the operator; content does not.

inference_location.value: Device first; then the person's vault-local model or a no-retention runtime we control (paid by credits); cloud only with the person's own key, called from the device straight to the vendor. Today BYOK is server-proxied, a known gap until phase (a).

supported_platforms.value: Native apps carry the strongest guarantee; on web the guarantee rests on trusting the code we serve, mitigated by signed or pinned builds.

update_trust.value: Native: store-signed builds. Web: an enforced CSP plus signed or pinned builds; the CSP is report-only today.

primary_copy_removal.value: All 18 EncryptedString columns that carry journal prose, DERIVED_FROM_PROSE plaintext, Creek copies, vendor copies and backups are re-encrypted client-side, withdrawn or expired before an account is labelled protected.

threat_actors.value: Defeats DB thief, backup holder, host, privileged operator and stored-data subpoena for stored content; a compelled web update and a compromised device remain; runtime-we-control inference is not operator-blind while it runs; until phase (a) our server relays BYOK calls and sees their plaintext.

reopen_triggers.value: Key-non-possession prototype fails; no web anchor is buildable; D03 user testing shows unacceptable loss; B09 finds no supported non-cloud configuration.
